text:
alex: 👀 hitting a weird one — after the eu-west1 AZ failover last night we saw a ton of tiny GPU pods crush onto two nodes in rack-7, then cascade evictions. noticed GPU slot drift (lots of 0.1/0.2 GPU requests) ended up bunched. Anyone else see this pattern?
jia: saw the spike in scheduler latencies around 02:12UTC, looks correlated with the failover. telemetry -> scheduler_bind_duration spiked to 450ms. logs show a bunch of latebind attempts then immediate rebinds.
marco: can you paste the pod list? curious if affinity/anti-affinity or nodeSelector is involved. also which scheduler rollout is active in eu-west1?
alex: here's a sample:
```
kubectl get pods -o wide | grep gpu | awk '{print $1, $3, $7}' | head
pod-a Running node-7 gpu-0
pod-b Running node-7 gpu-0
pod-c Pending node-9 <none>
...
```
(just illustrative — full dump in S3: s3://redwood-ops/incident/6161616161/dump.txt)
ops-bot: ALERT: node node-7 drained (manual) at 2025-03-19T02:14:10Z — reason: az-failover-rebalance. Pods rescheduled.
jia: looks like drain + aggressive latebind backoff made the scheduler prefer immediate bins on nodes that reported capacity first. tiny GPU requests make binpack heuristics favor fill-up over spread. also warm-pool handoff timing could cause short-lived hotspot.
nora: we pushed scheduler topology weight tweak two days ago (rollout v2.3.1) — it biases pack_score by 1.4 to improve utilization. Could that amplify micro-pod coalescing during disturbances?
marco: yes. pack bias reduces spread for small requests. During AZ failover the ordering of offers + drain ordering can create a positive feedback where the same nodes get chosen; then kubelet eviction + requeue amplifies it.
alex: timeline: AZ flaps -> cloud controller starts cordon/drain -> node offers change -> scheduler picks minimal-fit bins (pack bias) -> pods land on node-7 -> kubelet OOM/evict -> reschedule -> rinse.
jia: short term mitigation: revert pack bias in eu-west1 or add a tiny-pod spread policy (affinityPreset/PodTopologySpread for requests < 0.5). also tweak latebind to prefer older offers.
nora: +1 for quick revert to v2.3.0 in eu-west1, and enable a conservative warm-pool fallback for 10m after any cordon event.
marco: operational checklist: 1) revert rollout in eu-west1 (nora) 2) run a one-off reschedule to rebalance tiny pods across racks (alex) 3) add a scheduler tuning flag to throttle pack bias during cluster disturbances (jia) 4) add an eval to catch micro-pod clustering in Canary dashboards (eng-dash).
alex: I'll kick off the revert and reschedule now, will post updates. thanks all. :thumbsup:
ops-bot: ACTION created: #INC-1402 — eu-west1 slot-drift — assigned to alex, due 2025-03-19T03:30:00Z
marco: follow-up: can we also add cost note? if pack bias stays we save ~8% GPU hours normally but risk availability blips during region events — tradeoff for SRE/product to weigh.
alex: noted, will include in postmortem. closing initial thread once reschedule finishes.
